problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=3.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{2}{9\pi }M({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}).$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis.

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Radius of Gyration of a Plane Lamina

feedback.problem: A plate of mass $M$ occupies the circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}\le 6.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{9\pi }{y}^{2}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin.
feedback.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{6},\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

The moment of inertia about the origin, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{9\pi }{r}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{9\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}{r}^{5}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{9\pi }({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{9\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{6}}({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{9\pi }\cdot 36\cdot {[\frac{\theta }{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }{4}]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{9\pi }\cdot 36\cdot \pi  \\  & =4M.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{4M\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
